questions.question:
Simplify the following expression and identify its nature:

 (5sqrt{3} times sqrt{12}) / sqrt{2}
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

⇒ √12 = 2√3

⇒ 5√3 × 2√3 = 10 × 3 = 30

⇒ Expression becomes 30 / √2

⇒ Rationalize: (30√2)/2 = 15√2

**∴ Answer = 15√2**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** (5√3 × √12) / √2

**Formula:** √a × √b = √(ab)

⇒ 5√3 × √12 = 5 × √(3 × 12)

⇒ = 5 × √36 = 5 × 6 = 30

⇒ Expression = 30 / √2

⇒ Rationalizing denominator:

⇒ = (30 × √2) / (√2 × √2)

⇒ = (30√2) / 2 = 15√2

**Final Answer: 15√2 (Irrational Number)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

**1. Rationalization:** Removing root from denominator using multiplication. Example: a/√b = (a√b)/b

**2. Properties of Surds:** √a × √b = √(ab), helps in simplification

**3. Irrational Numbers:** Numbers that cannot be written as p/q. Example: √2, √3

**4. Perfect Squares:** √36 = 6, √49 = 7 — helps in quick solving

questions.question: Rational numbers are a subset of:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

⇒ Number system hierarchy: Natural ⊂ Whole ⊂ Integers ⊂ Rational ⊂ Real

⇒ Rational numbers lie inside Real numbers

⇒ So rational ⊂ real

**∴ Answer = Real numbers**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Rational numbers are a subset of ?

**Formula:** Rational number = p/q where q ≠ 0

⇒ All rational numbers can be expressed as fractions

⇒ Real numbers include both rational and irrational numbers

⇒ Hence, every rational number belongs to real numbers

**Final Answer: Real numbers**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

**1. Natural Numbers:** Counting numbers starting from 1

**2. Integers:** Include negative numbers, zero, and positive numbers

**3. Rational Numbers:** Numbers expressible as p/q (e.g., 1/2, −3)

**4. Real Numbers:** Combination of rational and irrational numbers

questions.question:
Riya drank 0.75 liters of water in the morning and 3(1)/(2) liter in the evening.

How much water did she drink in total?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

⇒ 0.75 = 3/4 and 3 1/2 = 7/2

⇒ Convert: 7/2 = 14/4

⇒ Total = 3/4 + 14/4 = 17/4 = 4.25

⇒ = 4.25 liters

**∴ Answer = 4.25 liters**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

0.75 liters and 3 1/2 liters

**Formula:**

Add quantities after converting into same form

**Calculation:**

⇒ 0.75 = 3/4

⇒ 3 1/2 = 7/2

⇒ LCM of 4 and 2 = 4

⇒ 3/4 + 7/2 = 3/4 + 14/4 = 17/4

⇒ 17/4 = 4.25 liters

**Final Answer: 4.25 liters**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

**1. Decimal to Fraction:** 0.75 = 3/4

**2. Mixed Fraction:** a b/c = (ac + b)/c

**3. Fraction Addition:** a/b + c/d = (ad + bc)/bd

**4. Conversion:** 17/4 = 4.25

questions.question: A runner completes 5(1/3) laps of a 400-meter track. Each lap takes 1.6 minutes. How many kilometres does the runner cover, and what is the total time taken?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

⇒ 5 1/3 = 16/3 laps

⇒ Distance = (16/3) × 400 = 6400/3 m = 2.133 km

⇒ Time = (16/3) × 1.6 = 25.6/3 = 8.5 min

**∴ Distance = 2.13 km, Time = 8.5 minutes**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Track length = 400 m

Laps = 5 1/3

Time per lap = 1.6 minutes

**Formula:**

Total Distance = Number of laps × Track length

Total Time = Number of laps × Time per lap

**Calculation:**

⇒ 5 1/3 = (5×3 + 1)/3 = 16/3

⇒ Distance = (16/3) × 400 = 6400/3 m

⇒ = 2133.33 m = 2.133 km

⇒ Time = (16/3) × 1.6

⇒ = 25.6/3 = 8.5 minutes

**Final Answer: Distance = 2.13 km, Time = 8.5 minutes**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

**1. Mixed Fraction Conversion:** a b/c = (ac + b)/c

**2. Unit Conversion:** 1000 m = 1 km

**3. Distance Formula:** Distance = Speed × Time

**4. Multiplication Trick:** Multiply whole first, then divide

questions.question: The square root of 169 is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The square root of 169 can be directly found using the property of perfect squares.

169 is a perfect square as 13 × 13 = 169.

**∴ Answer = 13**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** **Given:**

We need to find the square root of 169.

**Formula used:**

√N = a, where a × a = N

**Calculations:**

Step 1: Check factors of 169

⇒ 169 = 13 × 13

⇒ √169 = 13

**∴ The correct answer is 13 (Option 2).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Perfect Squares

A perfect square is a number that can be expressed as the square of an integer, e.g., 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, etc.

Square Root Property

The square root of a perfect square N is an integer a such that a × a = N.

Prime Factorization

To find the square root of a number, express it as the product of its prime factors, pair them, and multiply one factor from each pair.

questions.question: A box has marbles in the ratio 5:3:2 (red: green: blue). If there are 100 marbles in total, how many are green?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total ratio = 5 + 3 + 2 = 10

Green part = 3 (out of 10)

Green marbles = (3 ÷ 10) × 100

= 30

**∴ Answer = 30**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** 

**Given:**

Total marbles = 100

Ratio of red:green:blue = 5:3:2

**Formula used:**

Part value = (Required ratio part ÷ Total ratio) × Total quantity

 Red (5 parts) Green (3 parts) Blue (2 parts) = 50 = 30 = 20 

**Calculations:**

Total ratio = 5 + 3 + 2 = 10

⇒ Green marbles = (3 ÷ 10) × 100

⇒ Green marbles = 30

**∴ The correct answer is 30.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Ratio Basics

The ratio represents the relative values of quantities. Total parts are the sum of the ratio terms.

Unitary Method

To find the value of one part, divide the total by the sum of ratio terms and multiply by the required part.

Proportional Distribution

Quantities can be distributed proportionally using ratios to maintain balance in allocation.

questions.question: A train moves from City A to City B, a distance of 180 Kilometres in 3 hours. If the train keeps running at the same constant rate, how many hours will it take to travel the distance between City C and City D, which are 720 Kilometres apart?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

⇒ Distance becomes 4 times: 720/180 = 4

⇒ Time will also become 4 times

⇒ Required time = 3 × 4 = 12 hours

**∴ Answer = 12 hours**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance A→B = 180 km, Time = 3 hours

Distance C→D = 720 km

**Formula:**

Speed = Distance / Time

Time = Distance / Speed

**Calculation:**

⇒ Speed = 180 / 3 = 60 km/hr

⇒ Time = 720 / 60 = 12 hours

**Final Answer: 12 hours**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

**1. Speed Formula:** Speed = Distance / Time

**2. Direct Proportion:** At constant speed, time ∝ distance

**3. Unit Consistency:** Always keep km and hours consistent

**4. Scaling Trick:** If distance multiplies by n, time also multiplies by n

questions.question: Consider a sequence of five odd numbers that follow each other. If their average is 39, what is the value of the largest number in the sequence?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

⇒ Consecutive odd numbers → average = middle term

⇒ Middle number = 39

⇒ Sequence: 35, 37, 39, 41, 43

⇒ Largest = 43

**∴ Answer = 43**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

5 consecutive odd numbers with average = 39

**Formula:**

Average = Sum / Number of terms

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let numbers be: x−4, x−2, x, x+2, x+4

⇒ Average = x

⇒ x = 39

⇒ Largest number = x + 4 = 39 + 4 = 43

**Final Answer: 43**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

**1. Consecutive Odd Numbers:** Difference between terms = 2

**2. Symmetric Series:** Numbers equally spaced around middle

**3. Average Property:** Mean equals central value in AP

**4. General Form:** For 5 terms → x−4, x−2, x, x+2, x+4

questions.question: A number is increased by 20% and then decreased by 20%. What is the net change?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

⇒ Use direct formula: Net % change = a − b − (ab/100)

⇒ = 20 − 20 − (20×20)/100

⇒ = −4%

**∴ Answer = 4% decrease**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Increase = 20%, Decrease = 20%

**Formula:**

Successive change = Initial × (1 + a/100) × (1 − b/100)

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let initial value = 100

⇒ After 20% increase: 100 × 1.2 = 120

⇒ After 20% decrease: 120 × 0.8 = 96

⇒ Net change = 96 − 100 = −4

⇒ % change = −4%

**Final Answer: 4% decrease**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

**1. Successive Percentage:** a% increase and b% decrease → net = a − b − ab/100

**2. Important Result:** Equal increase and decrease always gives loss

**3. Shortcut Case:** x% up & x% down → loss = x²/100

**4. Example:** 20²/100 = 4% loss

questions.question: The income of A is 25% more than B's income, and B's income is 20% less than C's income. If A's income is ₹9,000, what is C's income?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

⇒ A = 125% of B ⇒ B = 9000 × (100/125) = 7200

⇒ B = 80% of C ⇒ C = 7200 × (100/80) = 9000

**∴ Answer = 9000**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

A = 25% more than B

B = 20% less than C

A = 9000

**Formula:**

If X is p% more than Y ⇒ X = Y × (1 + p/100)

If X is p% less than Y ⇒ X = Y × (1 − p/100)

**Calculation:**

⇒ A = 1.25B

⇒ 9000 = 1.25B ⇒ B = 9000 / 1.25 = 7200

⇒ B = 0.8C

⇒ 7200 = 0.8C ⇒ C = 7200 / 0.8 = 9000

**Final Answer: 9000**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

**1. Percentage Conversion:** 25% more ⇒ ×1.25, 20% less ⇒ ×0.8

**2. Reverse Calculation:** Divide when reversing percentage relation

**3. Chain Concept:** A → B → C relation solved stepwise

**4. Shortcut Tip:** Convert percentages into multipliers for speed

questions.question: A mobile phone worth ₹8,000 is sold at a loss of 10%. What is the selling price?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Loss % = 10% ⇒ Selling Price = Cost Price − (Loss % of Cost Price).

SP = 8000 − (10% of 8000).

10% of 8000 = 800 ⇒ SP = 8000 − 800 = 7200.

**∴ Answer = ₹7,200**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost Price = ₹8,000, Loss % = 10%

**Formula used:**

SP = CP − (Loss % × CP).

 
 Cost Price (₹8,000)
 
• 
 
 Selling Price (₹7,200)
 Loss ₹800

**Calculations:**

Loss = 10% of ₹8,000 = ₹800

⇒ SP = ₹8,000 − ₹800

⇒ SP = ₹7,200

**∴ The correct answer is ₹7,200 (Option 3).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Loss Percentage Formula

Loss % = (Loss ÷ Cost Price) × 100

Selling Price with Loss

SP = CP − Loss, where Loss = (Loss % × CP).

Profit and Loss Relationship

Profit or Loss is always calculated based on the Cost Price.

Marked Price and Discounts

For discounts, SP = MP − Discount, where Discount = (Discount % × MP).

questions.question: In a school, 60% of the students are boys. If the number of girls is 480, how many boys are there in the school?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Girls = 40% (since boys = 60%)

⇒ 40% = 480

⇒ 1% = 480 ÷ 40 = 12

⇒ Boys = 60% = 12 × 60 = 720

**∴ Answer = 720**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Percentage of boys = 60%

Percentage of girls = 40%

Number of girls = 480

**Formula:**

Part = (Percentage ÷ 100) × Total

**Calculations:**

⇒ 40% of total students = 480

⇒ Total = 480 ÷ 0.4 = 1200

⇒ Number of boys = 60% of 1200

⇒ = 0.6 × 1200 = 720

**∴ Number of boys = 720**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

**Percentage to Fraction:** x% = x ÷ 100, helps in quick conversion.

**Reverse Percentage:** If part is known, Total = Part ÷ (Percentage ÷ 100).

**Ratio Concept:** Boys : Girls = 60 : 40 = 3 : 2

**Unitary Method:** Find value of 1% first, then multiply to required percentage.

questions.question: If the marked price of an item is ₹1,500 and the selling price is ₹1,200, what is the percentage discount?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Discount = 1500 − 1200 = 300

⇒ 1500 corresponds to 100%

⇒ 300 corresponds to (300 ÷ 1500) × 100

⇒ = 20%

**∴ Answer = 20%**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = 1500

Selling Price (SP) = 1200

**Formula:**

Discount% = [(MP − SP) ÷ MP] × 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ Discount = 1500 − 1200 = 300

⇒ Discount% = (300 ÷ 1500) × 100

⇒ = (1 ÷ 5) × 100 = 20%

**∴ Percentage Discount = 20%**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

**Discount Formula:** Discount = MP − SP

**Successive Discount:** Net Discount = a + b − (ab ÷ 100)

**Marked Price Relation:** SP = MP − Discount

**Profit/Loss Link:** If SP > CP ⇒ Profit, if SP < CP ⇒ Loss

questions.question: A sofa is marked at ₹5,000 and sold for ₹4,250 after two successive discounts of 10% and a certain percentage. What is the second discount?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

After 10% discount ⇒ Price = 5000 × 0.9 = 4500

Final SP = 4250

⇒ Reduction = 4500 − 4250 = 250

⇒ Second discount = (250 ÷ 4500) × 100 ≈ 5.56%

**∴ Answer = 5.56%**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price = 5000

First discount = 10%

Selling Price = 4250

**Formula:**

SP = MP × (1 − d₁) × (1 − d₂)

**Calculations:**

⇒ 4250 = 5000 × 0.9 × (1 − d₂)

⇒ 4250 = 4500 × (1 − d₂)

⇒ (1 − d₂) = 4250 ÷ 4500 = 0.9444

⇒ d₂ = 1 − 0.9444 = 0.0556

⇒ d₂ = 5.56%

**∴ Second Discount = 5.56%**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

**Successive Discount Formula:** Net Discount = a + b − (ab ÷ 100)

**Multiplier Method:** Final Price = MP × (1 − d₁) × (1 − d₂)

**Approximation Trick:** Small discounts can be quickly estimated using ratio reduction.

**Important Insight:** Second discount always applies on reduced price, not on MP.

questions.question: A does a work in 10 days and B does the same work in 15 days. How much part of the work is completed in 2 days if they work together?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

LCM of 10 and 15 = 30 (Total Work)

⇒ A's efficiency = 30 ÷ 10 = 3

⇒ B's efficiency = 30 ÷ 15 = 2

⇒ Together = 3 + 2 = 5 units/day

⇒ In 2 days = 5 × 2 = 10 units = 10 ÷ 30 = 1 ÷ 3

**∴ Answer = 1 ÷ 3**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

A completes work in 10 days

B completes work in 15 days

**Calculations:**

⇒ Work done in 2 days = 5 × 2 = 10

⇒ Fraction of work = 10 ÷ 30 = 1 ÷ 3

**∴ Work completed = 1 ÷ 3**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

**LCM Advantage:** Converts fractional work into integers for faster calculation.

**Efficiency Rule:** Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

**Combined Efficiency:** Add efficiencies when working together.

**Work Fraction:** Work done = (Work completed ÷ Total work)

questions.question: A can do a task in 18 days, and B in 9 days. After working together for 4 days, A leaves. How many more days will B take to complete the remaining work?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

LCM of 18 and 9 = 18 (Total Work)

⇒ A = 1 unit/day, B = 2 units/day

⇒ Together = 3 units/day

⇒ In 4 days = 3 × 4 = 12 units

⇒ Remaining = 18 − 12 = 6 units

⇒ B alone time = 6 ÷ 2 = 3 days

questions.question: A train covers 180 km in 3 hours. How long will it take to cover 240 km at the same speed?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Speed same ⇒ Time ∝ Distance

⇒ 180 km ⇒ 3 hr

⇒ 240 km ⇒ (240 ÷ 180) × 3

⇒ = (4 ÷ 3) × 3 = 4 hr

**∴ Answer = 4 hours**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Distance = 180 km, Time = 3 hours

New distance = 240 km

**Formula:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time

Time = Distance ÷ Speed

**Calculations:**

⇒ Speed = 180 ÷ 3 = 60 km/hr

⇒ Time for 240 km = 240 ÷ 60 = 4 hours

**∴ Required time = 4 hours**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

**Speed Formula:** Speed = Distance ÷ Time

**Direct Proportion:** If speed is constant, Time ∝ Distance

**Unit Conversion:** Ensure km/hr consistency while calculating

**Shortcut Tip:** Use ratio method to avoid full speed calculation

questions.question: A train running at 72 km/h crosses a platform in 25 seconds. If the platform is 300 m long, what is the length of the train?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Speed = 72 km/hr = 20 m/s

⇒ Total distance in 25 sec = 20 × 25 = 500 m

⇒ Train + Platform = 500 m

⇒ Train length = 500 − 300 = 200 m

**∴ Answer = 200 m**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed = 72 km/hr

Time = 25 sec

Platform length = 300 m

**Formula:**

Speed (m/s) = Speed (km/hr) × 5 ÷ 18

Total distance = Speed × Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Speed = 72 × 5 ÷ 18 = 20 m/s

⇒ Distance covered = 20 × 25 = 500 m

⇒ Train length + Platform length = 500

⇒ Train length = 500 − 300 = 200 m

**∴ Length of train = 200 m**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

**Train Crossing Platform:** Total distance = Train length + Platform length

**Speed Conversion:** km/hr to m/s = × 5 ÷ 18

**Basic Formula:** Distance = Speed × Time

**Key Insight:** Crossing platform means full train passes entire platform

questions.question: A sum of ₹2,500 becomes ₹3,000 in 4 years at simple interest. What is the rate of interest?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Interest = 3000 − 2500 = 500

⇒ 4 years interest = 500

⇒ 1 year interest = 500 ÷ 4 = 125

⇒ Rate = (125 ÷ 2500) × 100 = 5%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = 2500

Amount (A) = 3000

Time (T) = 4 years

**Formula:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI = A − P = 3000 − 2500 = 500

⇒ 500 = (2500 × R × 4) ÷ 100

⇒ 500 = 100R

⇒ R = 5%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

**SI Formula:** SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

**Amount Relation:** A = P + SI

**Unitary Method:** Find 1 year interest, then compute rate

**Shortcut Tip:** Rate = (SI × 100) ÷ (P × T)

questions.question: A cone has a base radius of 6 cm and height of 8 cm. Find its volume (Take pi = 3.14).
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Volume of cone = (1 ÷ 3) × π × r² × h

⇒ = (1 ÷ 3) × 3.14 × 6² × 8

⇒ 6² = 36 ⇒ 36 × 8 = 288

⇒ = (1 ÷ 3) × 3.14 × 288 = 3.14 × 96

⇒ = 301.44 cm³

**∴ Answer = 301.44 cm³**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius (r) = 6 cm

Height (h) = 8 cm

π = 3.14

**Formula:**

Volume = (1 ÷ 3) × π × r² × h

 
• 
• 
• h = 8 r = 6 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Volume = (1 ÷ 3) × 3.14 × 6² × 8

⇒ = (1 ÷ 3) × 3.14 × 36 × 8

⇒ = (1 ÷ 3) × 3.14 × 288

⇒ = 3.14 × 96 = 301.44 cm³

**∴ Volume of cone = 301.44 cm³**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

**Cone Volume:** V = (1 ÷ 3) × π × r² × h

**Cylinder Volume:** V = π × r² × h

**Relation:** Cone volume is 1 ÷ 3 of cylinder (same base & height)

**Slant Height:** l = √(r² + h²)

questions.question: A solid hemisphere is melted and reshaped into a sphere of the same radius. How does the volume change?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Hemisphere volume = (2 ÷ 3)πr³

Sphere volume = (4 ÷ 3)πr³

⇒ Sphere = 2 × Hemisphere

⇒ So volume doubles

**∴ Answer = Volume becomes double**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

A solid hemisphere is reshaped into a sphere of same radius

**Formula:**

Volume of hemisphere = (2 ÷ 3)πr³

Volume of sphere = (4 ÷ 3)πr³

**Calculations:**

⇒ Hemisphere volume = (2 ÷ 3)πr³

⇒ Sphere volume = (4 ÷ 3)πr³

⇒ Ratio = Sphere : Hemisphere = (4 ÷ 3) : (2 ÷ 3) = 2 : 1

**Conclusion:**

⇒ Volume becomes double

**∴ Volume after reshaping = 2 times original**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

**Sphere Volume:** V = (4 ÷ 3)πr³

**Hemisphere Volume:** V = (2 ÷ 3)πr³

**Volume Conservation:** On melting, volume remains same unless reshaped differently

**Key Insight:** Two hemispheres make one sphere
